key_insight: Machine-learned molecular dynamics predicts that about 0.5% tensile strain drives MAPbI₃ from tetragonal to cubic at 300 K while increasing its band gap.
engineering_relevance: Finite-temperature strain modeling can guide epitaxial substrate selection to tune perovskite absorber phases and optical properties.
method: Train machine-learned force fields on-the-fly using DFT.
Run nanosecond bulk and free-standing slab simulations with fixed in-plane lattice vectors.
Track structural changes and average band gaps over MD snapshots.
evidence_signal: Bulk and slab models show consistent strain trends; the predicted phase transition agrees with experiments on KCl-supported films, and the band-gap blue shift matches the experimental trend.
watch_item: Static calculations on averaged structures predict the opposite band-gap trend, highlighting the need to sample finite-temperature disorder.
paper_title: Strain-Induced Tetragonal-to-Cubic Transition in MAPbI$_3$ from Machine-Learned Molecular Dynamics
